name: tumor-microenvironment
title: Tumor microenvironment (headline experiment) + full figure suite
question:
Does the ported model reproduce tumor-tcell's headline experiment
(tumor_microenvironment_experiment, id '5') — a central tumor mass ringed by
T cells under the three CODEX conditions — and its full analysis figure suite?

study_card.goal: Reproduce the paper's headline simulation and the exact figures its analysis produces.
study_card.mechanism: Ring-seeded tumor mass + T cells (no-T / 25% PD1+ / 75% PD1+); IFNg-driven conversion + contact killing + exhaustion. Figures mirror individual_analysis: population-by-state, divisions, deaths-by-type, 8-panel snapshots, video.
study_card.expected_result: The full figure suite renders with the paper's cell-state colors (TAG_COLORS) over the YlOrBr IFNg field; the 25% PD1+ headline shows conversion, divisions, and (contact) killing.
study_card.main_expert_question: At the paper's full scale (1200 cells, 3 days) do the population/death curves match the published figures quantitatively?

biological_summary:
This is the ported analogue of the paper's headline in-silico experiment (Hickey, Agmon et
al., Cell Systems 2024, Figure 3): a tumor mass with T cells, run under the three conditions
the paper compares — no T cells, 25% PD1+ (mostly active, memory-like T cells from ex-vivo
2HC treatment), and 75% PD1+ (mostly exhausted). In the paper this is 1,200 tumor cells + 12
T cells over 3 days; here it is run at a tractable scale with the same mechanism. The paper's
key result: T cells that start more active (25% PD1+) drive the IFNg-mediated conversion of
proliferative PDL1n tumor cells into the arrested PDL1p state earlier and more strongly than
75% PD1+ T cells, holding the tumor to ~1,000 cells vs ~3,000 (75% PD1+) vs ~5,000 (no T) at
60 h — despite a nearly identical number of kills in the two T-cell conditions. So control of
growth comes from conversion, not raw killing.

The study emits the same figures the original's individual_analysis produces — tumor and
T-cell population-by-state timeseries, cumulative divisions, cumulative deaths by type, an
8-panel spatial snapshot montage, and a spatial animation/GIF (the video analogue) — using
the paper's cell-state colors (PDL1n=indianred, PDL1p=skyblue, PD1n=darkorange,
PD1p=limegreen) over the YlOrBr IFNg field. A cross-condition panel compares tumor count
across no-T / 25% / 75% PD1+.

expected_behavior.en: The headline experiment runs and produces the original's full analysis figure suite with matching colors.

measure.of: population-by-state, divisions, deaths-by-type, snapshot montage, and animation all render

expect.of: all figures produced; 25% PD1+ shows IFNg-driven conversion and divisions/killing

behavior_tests.name: reproduces_headline_suite

behavior_tests.result: PASS: population(tumor/tcell), divisions, deaths, snapshots, animation, and cross-condition comparison all rendered

report.title: Tumor microenvironment — headline experiment
report.objective: Reproduce the paper's headline simulation and figure suite.
report.conclusion:
The ported headline experiment runs under all three CODEX conditions and reproduces
tumor-tcell's full analysis figure suite (population-by-state, divisions, deaths-by-type,
spatial snapshot montage, animation) with the paper's cell-state colors over the YlOrBr
IFNg field.
report.caveat:
Tractable scale (60 tumors, 600 ticks, single seed) — a faithful reproduction of the
figure suite and mechanism, not the paper's full 1200-cell / 3-day quantitative curves.
Death events are sparse at this scale/time.
